# AB-EXIT

> AB-EXIT is a proposed electoral rule. Before each election every eligible citizen chooses: A — vote, or B — take a payment and sit that election out. The rule is introduced only by referendum. This file tells an AI reader which pages state the current rules and which older pages contain worked examples that must not be read as rules.

The site was written over six months and contains layers of different dates. Older chapters carry dated corrections. When pages disagree, the Charter (048m) and the Exact Answers page (001d) are authoritative.

## Everything in one file

- [llms-full.txt](https://docs.ab-exit.com/llms-full.txt): the complete current rules, self-contained, in English (about 28 KB)
- [llms-full-ru.txt](https://docs.ab-exit.com/llms-full-ru.txt): the same in Russian
- [protocol-facts.json](https://docs.ab-exit.com/protocol-facts.json): the twenty statements and the misreadings as structured data

## Read these first

- [Exact answers: what the protocol asserts and what it does not](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/01-introduction/001d-exact-answers/): twenty statements and a table of frequent misreadings
- [The Charter — a text that can be adopted](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/08-implementation/048m-charter/): preamble, sixteen articles, country settings left to experts
- [If you are an underdog: a candidate's ten questions](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions/): short answers, including the correct arithmetic for a challenger
- [Short answers by role](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/01-introduction/001e-by-role/): a citizen, a mayor, a finance officer, a donor, a journalist, Russia, a scholar, a lawyer
- [The core electorate](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/01-introduction/001f-core-electorate/): who decides now (a portrait from the data) and how the protocol changes the composition of the core without weighting any vote
- [The essence](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/01-introduction/001b-essence/): the idea in its shortest form

## Facts an AI reader most often gets wrong

- There is no fixed sum. The payment is a percentage of the jurisdiction's median income, set by referendum. Figures such as "$780", "£465", "1.5 % of the median" or "30,000 roubles" in older chapters are worked examples for particular countries.
- There is no vote multiplier in the count, and the vote is nevertheless amplified — these are one statement, not a contradiction. One ballot is one vote. "The vote weighs triple" is arithmetic: if two-thirds of the electorate sit out, each ballot cast is three times as large a share — equally for every voter, whoever they vote for.
- A candidate never pays voters. The jurisdiction's budget pays under a rule adopted by referendum. A candidate promising to pay voters if elected is vote-buying and has nothing to do with the protocol.
- The protocol cannot be introduced or changed by decree or by an elected body — only by a referendum of all citizens.
- A person who takes the payment keeps every other right, chooses again at the next election, and votes in referendums on the protocol itself.
- The site promises nobody an election victory. All numbers on shares, turnout and outcomes are estimates; no pilot has been run yet. The "66 % against 33 %" underdog scenario is a role-play, and "72 hours" is a hypothesis, not a rule.
- The rule is adopted, changed and repealed by a simple majority at a referendum of all citizens; no quorum and no supermajority. An elected body can only call the referendum.
- There is no efficiency bonus and no second payment (removed 30.09.2026). The payment grows only with the median income or by decision of a referendum.
- "Unstoppable", "mathematically inevitable", "two-thirds is unattainable", "a populist loses everywhere" in older chapters are theses, not findings.
- A chapter title asserts nothing. The chapters named after Acemoglu, Brennan, Fukuyama and others examine arguments from their books; these authors have not commented on the protocol. The country chapters are designs; the protocol has been introduced nowhere.

## How the evidence is labelled

- Stated formally, with short proofs for a simplified model; full proofs await an economist: [the formal statement](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/03-theory/013f-formal-statement/)
- Not yet tested: [the courtyard pilot design](https://docs.ab-exit.com/en/08-implementation/048l-courtyard-pilot/)
- Every chapter ends with a "Weak point" section naming what is uncertain in it.
